dedupe_keys.name: toronto police service bicycle thefts open data

description: The Toronto Police Service publishes every reported occurrence that included the theft of a bicycle since 2014 on its open data hub. Coverage: the City of Toronto, about 40,600 occurrences at the time read, each with occurrence and report dates broken into year, month, day of week and hour, police division, location and premises type, bicycle make, model, type, speed, colour and cost, recovery status, primary offence, the 158 and 140 neighbourhood codes, and coordinates. Format and access: an ArcGIS Hub dataset with downloads, a dashboard, a code sheet and documentation, and an ArcGIS feature service. Licence and cost: free under the Open Government Licence - Ontario, which allows commercial use with attribution. Caveats: occurrences judged unfounded are excluded, data from reporting parties are preliminary and may not be verified and dates in downloads are in UTC. The records can be used to map theft risk at stations and bike parking and to include security as a cost in cycling route choice or bike parking siting models. It relates to Berlin's police bicycle theft data and BikeMaps.org hazard reports in the catalogue.
